text.p: VIENNA, July 15 (Reuter) The main stories in the Austrian press this Tuesday are:
KURIER
- Moody's Investors Service downgrades Bank Austria's long-term deposit and senior debt ratings to Aa2 from Aaa over uncertainty around Vienna City's liability.
- Eight out of 10 Austrians expect lower pensions, according to an opinion poll.
- The Austrian Nationalbank posted a better-than-expected budget outlook for the first half of 1997 at 18 million schillings in revenues and 12 million schillings expenditure.
DER STANDARD
- The conservative People's Party has unanimously voted unanimously in favour of NATO entry at a meeting of the party leadership.
- The Greens attacked the government's refugee policies as too restrictive.
- Road pricing for trucks may be introduced through the back door. Transport Minister Caspar Einem says the system could be in place on West and South motorways by 1998.
- The number of insolvencies in the first half dropped by 14.8 percent to 2,449 from 2,873.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Banks are selling index-linked bonds tailor-made to institutional investors while private investors are only being offered more innovative investment products upon demand.
DIE PRESSE
- The conservative People's Party lays out its vision of Austria's future security policy, and demands entry to NATO and the WEU.
- The cabinet is set to decide on the 1998 budget on July 24.
- Reform of EU regional aid could bring massive cuts to Austria, especially the province of Burgenland.
- Shares in Austrian Airlines makes big gains on the stock market. Synergies through cooperation with Lauda Air are bearing fruit earlier than expected.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- There are to be two types of social security in future: one for the self-employed and one for the non self-employed.
- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat is to visit Vienna on Tuesday.
- The General Director Adolf Wala of the Austrian National Bank says that Austria is on course to join the first wave of EMU.
- The government is to revise its concept for a technology offensive.
- The Austrian National Bank has protested against any attack on its pension reserves.
- Beer consumption has been falling almost every month since March and has declined to 4.7 million hectolitres in the first half of the year compared with 4.8 million last year.
